subject: Quick clarifications on subprocessors & cross-border wording for marketplace listing

Subject: Quick clarifications on subprocessors & cross-border wording for marketplace listing

Hi Connor / Vanessa (cc Laura),

We're finishing the copy for Acme's marketplace listing and need two short, customer-facing items from Redwood by EOD Thursday (May 6):

1) One-line plain-language snippet (1–2 sentences) explaining how Redwood handles subprocessors and where customers can find the published list.
2) One-line confirmation of cross-border safeguards we rely on for customers using the Hosted API (we've got EU customers who will need to see what guarantees exist).

Small ask — two short variants would be ideal: a concise marketing-friendly line and a slightly more technical/legal alternate we can link to from the listing.

I've attached the marketplace brief with the character limits. Can you also confirm whether the subprocessor map we link to is the public page or a downloadable CSV? Finally, if there's any DPA short-blurb you prefer we surface, please include it.

Thanks — urgent because the marketplace intake deadline is 2026-05-06.

Best,
Sarah Jenkins
Senior Contracts Manager, Acme Corp

Subject: Re: Quick clarifications on subprocessors & cross-border wording for marketplace listing

Hi team — draft copy below. Kept everything short (<=220 chars where possible). I'm attaching a small markdown with three alternate snippets and a CSV export of the subprocessor list for the marketplace intake if they prefer a download.

Suggested snippets (pick one marketing + one technical):

- Marketing-friendly (concise): "Redwood partners with a limited set of subprocessors to operate our Hosted API; our up-to-date public subprocessor list and DPA information are available at redwood.ai/subprocessors."

- Legal-lite (slightly technical): "Redwood acts as a processor under a Data Processing Addendum (DPA). We publish our subprocessors and the technical and organisational safeguards we use for cross-border transfers at redwood.ai/subprocessors."

- Technical (for console/helptext): "Hosted API requests are processed in our US and EU regions. We rely on contractual safeguards (EU Standard Contractual Clauses or equivalent) and a public subprocessor map; customers can request a DPA."

Notes and asks:
- Subprocessor link: recommend surfacing https://redwood.ai/subprocessors (public page) as the canonical link for marketplace. We can optionally attach a CSV if the intake prefers a file.
- DPA blurb: "We process customer data as a processor under a DPA; customers can request a signed DPA and pin data residency for supported regions."
- Avoid jargon: prefer spelling out "EU Standard Contractual Clauses" in the marketplace line; use the acronym (SCCs) only in technical contexts.

Attachments: marketplace_snippets_v1.md, subprocessor_map_export.csv

Laura / Vanessa — can you confirm the residency phrasing ("pin data residency for supported regions") is accurate operationally? If the product team prefers different wording, I'll swap it out.

Thanks,
Karthik
Director, Product & Privacy, Redwood Inference
From: Sarah Jenkins <sarah.jenkins@acme.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Quick clarifications on subprocessors & cross-border wording for marketplace listing

Connor / Karthik — this is great, thanks for the quick turnaround. The three options give us good flexibility. Two tiny asks before we publish: 

1) Can the marketing-friendly line explicitly call out Hosted API? Our listing template has a "Service" field and we want the sentence to read as a direct statement about the Hosted API.
2) For the technical line, can you add the short parenthetical "(processed in our US and EU regions)" after Hosted API so customers know residency is available.

If you can send a final one-liner for each (marketing + technical) we'll slot them into the marketplace form. Deadline unchanged — we're publishing May 6.

Appreciate it — Sarah
Sarah Jenkins
Senior Contracts Manager, Acme Corp
